findings.detail: No chain step cites anything (evidence [] on all three); the run's five citations are only hypothesis-level supporting_evidence, so every statement here rests on citations moved down to the step.
All three chain subjects are kind 'other' with no CURIE and compound free text ('Dysregulated TREM2 signaling via MS4A4A'); only the object, Alzheimer disease, is grounded.

Every step is leads_to with polarity unknown, though each mechanism states a direction; all five statement signs come from the mechanisms, each backed by a cited text (sign_note), none from the chain.

The one step starts at 'Microglial innate immune dysfunction' and names none of TREM2, PLCG2 or ABI3, so none of the three gene claims has a route; the title's 'TREM2-PLCG2-ABI3 signaling cascade' never appears as a chain.

MS4A4A and INPP5D appear only inside the subject labels ('via MS4A4A', 'via INPP5D repression'): each single step packs gene -> process -> disease, which I split into two statements so the gene is a node.

PMID:28714976 reports the PLCG2 variant rs72824905 (p.Pro522Arg) as protective (OR 0.68), while the mechanism says rare coding variants in TREM2, PLCG2 and ABI3 alike impair immunity and accelerate AD.

Read literally, PMID:28714976 says the microglia-mediated innate immune response 'contributes directly to the development' of AD, so its dysfunction would protect; the mechanism says dysfunction accelerates AD (the paper means involvement, and its own variants go both ways).

The run lists no contradicting evidence anywhere, yet its own citations disagree on microglial innate immunity: PMID:28714976 has it contributing to AD development, PMID:41785844 (cited for hyp2) calls microglial responses protective; S1 holds both.
R-HSA-2172127 is a Reactome over-representation result ('DAP12 interactions', 3 of 52 entities) of the input genes; it states no step and does not show a TREM2-PLCG2-ABI3 cascade.
R-HSA-2424491 is a Reactome over-representation result ('DAP12 signaling', 2 of 36 entities) of the input genes; it states no step and says nothing about MS4A4A.

The mechanism claims 'accelerating Alzheimer disease progression', but the step says leads_to AD and the only paper is a case-control (risk) study; curated as progression, so hyp1's TREM2 claim cannot borrow hyp2's TREM2 -> AD risk statement.
No cited text says the variants impair microglial innate immunity or reduce clearance of amyloid plaques or debris; PMID:28714976 reports associations and an immune protein-interaction network only.
support 'grounded', confidence medium, for a chain whose one step is uncited, unsigned and ungrounded, and whose cited GWAS contradicts the mechanism for PLCG2.
hyp2 rests on a one-paragraph Neuron preview (PMID:41785844) of Rosner et al.; the primary paper is not cited, so both its arms stand on review evidence.
No cited text states the mechanism's 'AD risk alleles in MS4A4A further suppressing TREM2 activity'; PMID:41785844 says only that MS4A4A and MS4A6A are 'linked to Alzheimer's disease risk'.
The mechanism runs through RIPK1 kinase and PMID:41633359 states it (INPP5D's SH2 domain binds RIPK1 at p-Y383 to suppress RIPK1 kinase activation), but the chain has no RIPK1 node.

PMID:41633359's in vivo outcomes are neuronal TDP-43 pathology, neuronal loss and motor dysfunction, not amyloid or AD; its link to LOAD is 'Our data suggest' (kind hypothesis), so the INPP5D arm has no weight at the disease end.
APOE, the strongest common AD risk gene in the input, is left in unexplained_genes with RNPS1 and LPIN2; no hypothesis touches it.
The falsification knocks out TREM2, PLCG2 and ABI3 together and reads plaque load, so it cannot test the per-gene claims, nor the opposite direction of the protective PLCG2 variant.

hyp2's falsification (MS4A4A overexpression, TREM2 phosphorylation in iPSC microglia) and hyp3's (INPP5D knockdown, proinflammatory mediators in a microglial line) test only the gene -> process half (S2, S4), never the process -> Alzheimer disease half, which is where both arms are weakest (S3 a preview's qualifier, S5 a proposal).

An unsigned causal effect: all three steps are leads_to with no sign, and BioLean's only unsigned form is assoc, so each sign had to come from the run's mechanism plus a cited text that agrees (for S1 the cited texts disagree, so the mechanism picked which supports and which refutes).

When the step's polarity is unknown but the run's mechanism states a direction, the guide takes the sign from a cited text; for hyp1.1 the run's two cited texts disagree (PMID:28714976 literally +, PMID:41785844 protective), and the guide does not say whether the mechanism counts as 'the run's sign'. The curator took hyp1's own text (+, against the mechanism); the audit took the mechanism's direction (no_sign is 'no direction anywhere', and 'the sign is the run's'), so S1 is neg and PMID:28714976 refutes.

'X via <the hypothesis's own gene>': the guide collapses 'X via Y' to X (mechanism in passing) and splits only parallel compounds; I split serially (gene -> X, X -> disease) because the gene is the point of the step.

'Dysfunction' is in neither the loss-of-function list (loss, reduced, impaired, deficiency) nor the undirected one (dysregulates, abnormal); I read 'Microglial innate immune dysfunction' as impairment because the mechanism says 'impair'.
Direction given by a qualifier: PMID:41785844 calls the responses TREM2 drives 'protective' in AD; I took that as a signed effect on AD (S3 and S1 support), but the guide has no rule for it.

Late-onset Alzheimer disease (LOAD) has no fitting MONDO term in the corpus: MONDO:0007089 'Alzheimer disease 2' lists 'late onset Alzheimer disease' as a synonym but is defined as APOE E4-associated AD, and the generic term is NCIT:C195946 only; I took LOAD as Alzheimer disease, and the exclusion table has parent_disease for a broader disease but nothing for a narrower one.
Hypothesis-level supporting_evidence that no step cites has no slot of its own; each hypothesis here has one step, so I judged those citations under it (moved_from the hypothesis id).

PMID:41633359's abstract never names the organism or whether 'cell-autonomously' means cultured cells; I set mechanistic, taxon mouse, from its mouse gene symbols (Nlrp3, Zbp1) and aging knockout phenotypes.

A one-paragraph preview of a single primary paper counts as review, like a broad review: alone it gives S3 (TREM2 -> AD risk) belief 3/5, and on S1 its copy outweighs the 85,133-subject GWAS that refutes it (b 3/7, d 2/7): a single-paper preview counts more than the GWAS.
